newsitem.title: CHINA: China short on details of Taiwan shipping links.
newsitem.headline: China short on details of Taiwan shipping links.

text.p: Chinese officials on Thursday declined to clarify plans for direct shipping links with Taiwan, describing a deal hammered out in Hong Kong as a reference point for the rival governments.
Non-government representatives of the two sides, meeting in the British colony on Wednesday, reached what they called a consensus on ending a decades-old ban on direct shipping links.
"These are non-government organisations," said a Ministry of Communications spokesman, referring to the negotiating bodies that forged the agreement.
"Whatever they discuss has to be used as a reference point. It is designed to give government agencies something to rely on," he told Reuters.

The spokesman would not comment on specifics of the future shipping links, such as what flags would be flown by ships operating the route which would link Taiwan's port of Kaohsiung with the mainland ports of Fuzhou and Xiamen.
An official of the Taiwan Affairs Office of the State Council, or cabinet, also declined to comment on the accord, saying: "We have not been authorised to speak on this matter."
The semi-official Chinese Association for Relations Across the Taiwan Strait, which in the past has been a conduit for discussions with the island, also had no comment.

Taipei's chief negotiator at the talks was quoted by Taiwan media as saying shipping companies which had already received permission from Taiwanese authorities could now apply to China to sail directly between the island and the mainland.
Taiwan and China have been rivals since the end of the Chinese civil war in 1949.
China regards the island as a renegade province. Taiwan has banned direct links with China although it has allowed indirect trade, much of it through Hong Kong.
The British colony's return to Chinese rule on July 1 has pressured Taiwan to reach an understanding on direct links with its old adversary.
